title: Natural history and influencing factors of genetic developmental disorders and epilepsies
summary:
Background:
What is a genetic neurodevelopmental disorder or epilepsy?
A genetic disorder is caused by an alteration in the genes of affected individuals. Genes serve as the blueprint for the human body and are responsible, among other things, for encoding proteins. These proteins are essential for proper brain function, including the ability of nerve cells to communicate with one another. If a genetic alteration disrupts this process, it can result, for example, in the very early onset of epilepsy (seizures) and severe intellectual and physical disability. As these genetic alterations are exceedingly rare, it is of great importance to collect comprehensive information in order to advance our understanding of these conditions.

Research Objectives:
- Standardized assessment of the disease course of genetic neurodevelopmental disorders and epilepsies
- Long-term documentation of the disease trajectories of individuals affected by a genetic neurodevelopmental disorder and/or epilepsy, with the aim of improving the understanding of these rare conditions
- Investigation of the relationship between the genetic diagnosis (the underlying genetic alteration) and the clinical phenotype (disease characteristics/symptoms)

Methodology:
This study will retrospectively and longitudinally collect and analyze clinical and genetic data from individuals with genetic neurodevelopmental disorders and/or epilepsy over a period of ten years, drawing on routine clinical documentation and compiling the data in a database and/or spreadsheet. The following aspects will be assessed within the framework of this study:
- Disease phenotype (e.g., epilepsy, childhood development, additional symptoms, comorbidities)
- Clinical findings (e.g., genetic investigations, EEGs, MRIs)
- Treatment (pharmacological and non-pharmacological therapies)
